cohort: Women who underwent peripartum hysterectomy in Tehran, Iran, between March 2021 and March 2022, with gestational age greater than 24 weeks and the hysterectomy performed during delivery or within the first 24 hours postpartum.
finding: The primary indications for peripartum hysterectomy were placenta abnormalities (75.6%), uterine atony (20.7%), and uterine rupture (3%), with placenta previa (42.6%) and placenta accreta (32.4%) being the most common placental issues.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was the predominant delivery method (93.4%) in peripartum hysterectomy cases, and a previous Cesarean section was reported in 65.4% of these cases.
